title: KPN Newsletter Archive
bodyHtml:
Welcome to the quarterly update from the Knowledge Portal Network (KPN) which highlights production release updates, collaboration opportunities, funding opportunities, and upcoming events.

 

Spring 2026 Release

Production Release

Check out the latest Spring 2026 production releases for the following portals:

The Common Metabolic Diseases Knowledge Portal (CMDKP) includes several new features:

  • Download bottom line data for your phenotype of interest
  • View most significant Common Fund Data Ecosystem (CFDE) gene sets connected to your phenotype of interest

The Association to Function Knowledge Portal (A2FKP) includes 83 new genetic datasets and 21 new traits.

The Common Fund Data Ecosystem (CFDE) Knowledge Center has new features designed to expose scientific connections across CFDE through a user's research context. See the Tech Talk below for more details.

 

Other resources the KPN collaborates to build: 

Unique to PanKbase is the Integrated Maps of Pancreatic Islets where users can explore single cell maps; Data Library with harmonized meta-data and data from ~3500 donors.

 

Collaborate with KPN

Want to build your own Community Portal?

The Knowledge Portal team specializes in partnering with biomedical researchers to build resources, tailored to each research community, that will accelerate their research. We welcome new collaborations.

Contribute your data!

 

Research Roundup

Research advances are what drive our knowledge portals. Explore the ongoing work within our community.

The “bottom-line” associations: a scientific saga

By: Trang Nguyen

It’s been almost two centuries since Gregor Mendel gifted the world with his stories about the humble peas, and almost two decades since the first major genome-wide association studies (GWAS) of seven common diseases were published. Despite certain doubts about their utility, it is undeniable that GWAS provide valuable first clues in our search for disease culprits, as showcased by the guilty verdicts of NOD2 in Crohn’s disease and TCF7L2 in type 2 diabetes.

Read more.

 

Portal Spotlights

These portals are resources built hand-in-hand with scientific communities, bringing together data, tools, and domain expertise to enable collaborative research and new insights.

The Mammalian Adipose Tissue Knowledge Portal (MATKP) is an open community resource for adipose biology across multiple mammalian species.

Browse and explore 85 curated adipose tissue datasets across species, depots, assays, and experimental methods.

Introducing the Skin Knowledge Portal (Skin KP), which is advancing our understanding of skin disease through large-scale genomic data. This portal is being developed by international network of scientists and clinicians collaborating to advance our understanding of the genetic underpinnings of skin diseases by leveraging large-scale genetic and genomic data in collaboration with the KPN team. This effort is led by PIs Lavinia Paternoster (University of Bristol), Lynn Petukhova (NYU Langone Health), and Michael Simpson (King's College London).

 

Tech Talk

Explore newly released tools and platform improvements from across our portals, built to support researchers in accessing, analyzing, and interpreting complex biomedical data.

 

CFDE-REVEAL

Reasoning Engine for Validating Evidence Across the Landscape

CFDE-REVEAL connects your research question to hidden biological connections across 15+ Common Fund programs. First, the engine takes free-text search questions and extracts genes, mechanisms, and phenotypes to query CFDE data via semantic search. The Baysiean Model (PIGEAN) then estimates the probability genes are involved in disease using GWAS and gene set evidence. Then, the LLM selects relevant mechanisms, generates hypotheses, and suggests actionable next steps.

Turn mechanistic leads into experiments
CFDE-DESIGN is the follow-through — it builds on hypotheses from REVEAL to recommend experimental next steps, such as:
-plausible assays (e.g., RNA-seq, proteomics, CRISPR perturbation)
-relevant cell or tissue contexts
-candidate biomarkers or interventions
-CFDE datasets suited for validation

 

CMDKP Single-Cell Browser

Single-Cell Browser
Integrated human tissue reference maps developed using single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) from projects funded by the Foundation for the National Institutes of Health (FNIH) and additional external sources. Currently the portal represents 10 reference maps spanning Artery, Heart, Hypothalamus, Kidney, Liver, Muscle Structure, White Adipose Tissue, Tendon, and Islet of Langerhans.

Explore here.

Provide Feedback on the SysBio FAIRplex Ecosystem

Want to contribute to the development of the SysBio FAIRplex ecosystem, a transformative initiative under the NIH Common Fund Venture Program? SysBio FAIRplex is designed to integrate phenotypic, molecular, and clinical data across various Accelerating Medicines Partnership® (AMP®) programs, supporting groundbreaking research in systems biology, biomedical science, and omics studies.

We are currently seeking individuals—both AMP and non-AMP researchers, as well as experts and enthusiasts in large-scale systems biology, biomedical research, and omics studies—who may be interested in providing feedback to help shape this innovative ecosystem.

Complete feedback survey.

Funding Opportunities

Pilot Projects Enhancing Utility and Usage of Common Fund Data Sets (R03 Clinical Trial Not Allowed)

Many valuable and widely available data sets have been generated by multiple Common Fund programs. The purpose of this NOFO is to announce the availability of funding to demonstrate and enhance the utility of selected Common Fund data sets, including generating hypotheses and catalyzing discoveries. Award recipients are asked to provide feedback on the utility of the Common Fund data resources.

Apply before June 23rd, 2026
